steps.what: Determine required fonts, graphics and color separations from the approved specification
Adjust digital files using the specified edits and separation settings
Check adjusted elements and release the exact production file

tasks.design: Configure approved edit profiles in the prepress editor {OTHER}. The operator identifies the requested changes, reviews all edits against the specification in {DOCS}, and releases the exact corrected production file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated technical edits take time, while ambiguous artwork changes still need judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native file preflight and editing profiles can apply repeatable technical corrections.
tasks.still_hard: Font substitution, colour intent and changes that exceed the customer's approval.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a technically valid correction changes intended appearance or meaning.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive editing, with unchanged responsibility for visual correctness.

evidence.claim: Enfocus PitStop preflights and edits print files; Switch automates job flow.
The proposed operator-edit savings are an unmeasured scenario, not a transfer of the vendor's full prepress case result.

assumptions: Boundary covers file edits and operator release, not initial artwork creation, customer approval or press setup.

The operator produces source version, required edits, target colour profile, permitted substitutions and output requirements in s1; all30 hours remain counted. Unclear instructions require manual clarification before editing.
Use native edit profiles before custom code. Operator review and bespoke corrections remain in s2; no creative judgement is treated as deterministic.
Customer-significant changes require upstream customer approval; production release here only covers changes within the approved specification.
unknowns: Share of edits eligible for repeatable profiles
Installed editor capabilities and approved colour standards
research_questions: Do repeated technical edits save time after proof comparison and exception correction?

approvals.approved_version: Exact adjusted production file, change log and specification version; subsequent edits void release

steps.what: Direct press crews and monitor their work against job needs and safe practice

tasks.design: Keep live crew direction with the operator. Job information remains accessible in {OPS_SYSTEM}, but no new monitoring or instruction automation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Direction depends on live machine conditions and the crew's understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing job visibility can support the conversation but does not replace it.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting unsafe practice and resolving misunderstandings during production.
tasks.altitude: No change to crew leadership or attention required.

evidence.claim: Live crew direction remains unchanged; the digest does not establish a crew-supervision labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is live crew guidance, not workflow scheduling or individual productivity reporting.
No machine action relies on an assumed structured observation of crew activity.
Native job visibility is sufficient; no custom build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool or procedure is introduced.
unknowns: Crew responsibilities and local safety procedures
research_questions: Which handover misunderstandings require better human coordination?

steps.what: Identify completed jobs and select the final files and replication settings
Download completed jobs to the designated archive and retain their manifest
Check archive completeness, retrieval and failed downloads

tasks.design: Configure the existing print workflow {OTHER} to copy manifest-listed files into {DOCS} and log transfer results. The operator still selects the final versions and checks that the package supports later retrieval; failed transfers return to manual copying.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operators repeatedly locate and copy the same approved production assets.
tasks.enabler_now: Native print-flow automation can move files deterministically without deciding which version is final.
tasks.still_hard: Missing linked assets, obsolete fonts and settings needed to reproduce an old job.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether an archive contains enough context for safe replication.
tasks.altitude: Less copying, with unchanged final-version and retrieval responsibility.

evidence.claim: Enfocus Switch automates print job flow; the proposed archive completeness and labour scenario require local testing.
Manifest-driven archive transfer and the savings range are model-knowledge proposals.

assumptions: Boundary includes selecting, copying and checking completed jobs, not production or ongoing storage-system runtime.

Press operator produces job ID, completion state, exact source paths and versions, asset list, settings reference and destination in s1; all35 hours include this capture. There is no assumed free completed-job flag.
s2 consumes only the verified manifest. Missing files or uncertain versions stop copying and are resolved manually in s3; retry work is retained there.
Test native flow configuration first; no source deletion or automatic retention expiry is proposed.
unknowns: Native archive support and actual manual transfer effort
research_questions: Can a sampled archived job be restored with all required assets and settings?

incremental.description: Archive-rule checks and periodic restoration sampling

steps.what: Verify job readiness, machine availability and production constraints for scheduling
Build workflow scheduling options and update job tracking in the database
Resolve production conflicts and release the operational schedule

tasks.design: Test native scheduling and tracking in {OPS_SYSTEM} before adding a deterministic planning board. Use verified job constraints to propose feasible sequences; the operator resolves conflicts and releases the schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated sequencing and status updates consume time when constraints sit across job records.
tasks.enabler_now: Rules can check due dates, machine eligibility and material readiness without modelling commercial judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Rush orders, uncertain completion times and competing customer commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which commitment to renegotiate when no feasible schedule exists.
tasks.altitude: Less board maintenance; operational priorities remain human decisions.

reach.task: Reconcile machine capacity with delivery promises

evidence.claim: Deterministic print scheduling and job-board integration are model-knowledge designs; the digest's MIS source does not establish scheduling capability or measured savings.

assumptions: Boundary covers scheduling and job tracking, not crew supervision or creation of customer orders. Roll-ups assign each status-capture action once.

Operator verifies job ID, due date, quantity, machine eligibility, material readiness, current completion state and availability in s1; its35 hours include manual capture and correction. Upstream order staff retain their existing job-ticket production; no new free structured input is presumed.
Missing or stale status blocks automatic sequencing and uses the retained manual work in s2 and s3. No inferred readiness or individual performance scoring.
Native scheduling configuration is tested before custom rules; existing database runtime earns no saving.
research_questions: How often do missing readiness fields or infeasible constraints require manual rescheduling?
